# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  eval:
    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        sandbox = true
      # Pinned the same way nix-home.yml pins its attic-client: the image ships
      # no coreutils/grep/jq, and the test scripts in tests/ assume a normal
      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch
      # below. Any host with a full desktop config will do.
      TEST_HOST: utsuho
    steps:
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      # Do NOT echo $FORGE_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: authorise git against the private input
        env:
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".username oauth2
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".helper \
            '!f() { test "$1" = get && printf "password=%s\n" "$FORGE_TOKEN"; }; f'

      # The whole contract with `hmeval` is this file plus the two markers
      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".
      - name: run the request
        env:
          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu

          req=.hmeval-request
          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
            case "$k" in
              mode)  mode=$v ;;
              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
              tests) tests=$v ;;
              attr)  attr=$v ;;
            esac
          done < "$req"

          echo "hmeval: mode=$mode"
          echo "---8<--- hmeval"
          rc=0

          # $hosts and $tests are unquoted in the loops below ON PURPOSE: they
          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.
          # Quoting them turns the whole list into one argument, which fails as
          # "attribute 'utsuho fujiwara ...' missing" rather than as a syntax
          # error, so it looks like a broken flake instead of a broken quote.
          # hmeval guarantees they contain no other whitespace.

          case "$mode" in
            eval)
              # --no-link/--raw keeps this to evaluation plus whatever IFD the
              # config genuinely needs; nothing is pushed anywhere.
              for h in $hosts; do
                if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#homeConfigurations.$h.activationPackage.drvPath"); then
                  printf '  %-10s %s\n' "$h" "$out"
                else
                  printf '  %-10s FAILED\n' "$h"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            attr)
              if out=$(nix eval --raw ".#$attr"); then
                printf '  %s\n' "$out"
              else
                printf '  FAILED: .#%s\n' "$attr"
                rc=1
              fi

# Ad-hoc evaluation and test runs on the in-cluster runner, so a "does this
# still evaluate?" check costs nothing on the laptop.
#
# Driven by `hmeval --ci` (home.nix), which commits the working tree — dirty or
# not — to an `eval/**` branch and reads the result back out of this job's log.
# The branch is throwaway and `hmeval` deletes it afterwards.
#
# This does NOT push to attic. nix-home.yml owns the closure cache; this job
# only answers a question, so a scratch eval cannot poison the cache with paths
# built from a commit that never reached master.
name: nix-eval

on:
  push:
    branches: ["eval/**"]
  workflow_dispatch:

# Unlike nix-home.yml, this one cancels. A closure build that gets discarded
# wastes twenty minutes of work someone is waiting on; a superseded eval is
# just a stale answer, and `hmeval` is already watching the newer run.
concurrency:
  group: nix-eval-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  eval:
    # Same runner and image as nix-home.yml, for the same reasons — see
    # docs/ci-nix-home.md before changing either. In particular: no `uses:`
    # steps (the image has no node), and no awk/sed/grep, which is why the
    # request file below is parsed in pure bash.
    runs-on: privileged
    container:
      image: nixos/nix@sha256:1a711b619c8a713eff32c3f8d8781b3b4d0130cb91c0a57f67e87abfeeb90b01
    env:
      NIX_CONFIG: |
        experimental-features = nix-command flakes
        netrc-file = /root/.config/nix/netrc
        extra-substituters = http://attic.attic.svc.cluster.local/kube
        extra-trusted-public-keys = kube:REDACTED
        max-jobs = 6
        cores = 4
        sandbox = true
      # Pinned the same way nix-home.yml pins its attic-client: the image ships
      # no coreutils/grep/jq, and the test scripts in tests/ assume a normal
      # userland. One rev for both, so a bump moves them together.
      TOOLS_REV: 29916453413845e54a65b8a1cf996842300cd299
      # Which host tests/ should believe it is running on; see the tests branch
      # below. Any host with a full desktop config will do.
      TEST_HOST: utsuho
    steps:
      - name: authorise nix against attic
        env:
          ATTIC_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ATTIC_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p /root/.config/nix
          umask 077
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.attic.svc.cluster.local "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            > /root/.config/nix/netrc
          printf 'machine %s password %s\n' \
            attic.ko.ag "$ATTIC_TOKEN" \
            >> /root/.config/nix/netrc

      - name: checkout
        run: |
          set -eu
          git clone https://forge.ko.ag/${{ github.repository }}.git .
          git checkout --detach ${{ github.sha }}
          git --no-pager log -1 --oneline

      # Do NOT echo $FORGE_TOKEN or enable `set -x` here.
      - name: authorise git against the private input
        env:
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".username oauth2
          git config --global credential."https://forge.ko.ag".helper \
            '!f() { test "$1" = get && printf "password=%s\n" "$FORGE_TOKEN"; }; f'

      # below. Keep them in step: hmeval slices the job log between them, so a
      # renamed marker silently turns every run into "no output".
      - name: run the request
        env:
          # Load-bearing, and not obviously so. The credential helper configured
          # in the previous step answers out of $FORGE_TOKEN *at the moment nix
          # shells out to git*, which is here — so a helper installed globally
          # but an env set only on the earlier step leaves this one answering
          # with an empty password. The failure is not an auth error either; it
          # surfaces as `error: Failed to fetch git repository
          # 'https://forge.ko.ag/sauyon/dotfiles-private.git'` partway down a
          # stack trace about home.activation, which reads like a broken config.
          # nix-home.yml sets it on its build step for exactly this reason.
          FORGE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGE_TOKEN }}

          set -eu

          req=.hmeval-request
          if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
            echo "no $req in this commit — nothing to run."
            echo "This workflow is driven by \`hmeval --ci\`; pushing an eval/**"
            echo "branch by hand does not carry a request."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Pure bash: no awk/sed/grep in this image. Values are single-line by
          # construction (hmeval rejects newlines before it writes the file).
          mode=; hosts=; tests=; attr=
          while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
            case "$k" in
              mode)  mode=$v ;;
              hosts) hosts=$v ;;
              tests) tests=$v ;;
              attr)  attr=$v ;;
            esac

          # are space-separated lists and the word splitting is the mechanism.

                fi

                rc=1
              fi
              ;;

              # `homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname)` — fine on a box that
              # is one of the hosts, useless in a container whose hostname is
              # its own ID. Run 137 died twice over with
              #
              #   does not provide attribute
              #   'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4.config.home.packages'
              #
              # Rather than teach eight scripts a new seam, tell the ephemeral
              # container it is a host. It only ever needs to be *a* host whose
              # config contains the script under test; utsuho has all of them.
              printf '%s' "$TEST_HOST" > /etc/hostname
              echo "  (as $TEST_HOST)"

              # tests/*.sh are ordinary shell: they want coreutils, grep, sed
              # and jq, none of which the nix image has. Run them inside a
              # pinned shell rather than teaching each script to cope.
              tools="github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$TOOLS_REV"
              for t in $tests; do
                echo "  === $t"
                if nix shell \
                     "$tools#bash" "$tools#coreutils" "$tools#gnugrep" \
                     "$tools#gnused" "$tools#gawk" "$tools#git" \
                     "$tools#jq" "$tools#diffutils" \
                     -c bash "$t"; then
                  echo "  === $t PASSED"
                else
                  echo "  === $t FAILED"
                  rc=1
                fi
              done
              ;;
            *)
              echo "  unknown mode: $mode"
              rc=1
              ;;
          esac

          echo "---8<--- end"
          exit $rc

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile the two would collide.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# No sandbox between the caller and the CLI: a plain exec of node, so
+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.
+if grep -q 'exec .*/bin/node ' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" && ! grep -q bwrap "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
+
+# Under plain node, `orca-ide open` has no Orca binary to spawn but
+# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).
+# Exactly the profile's GUI: the unwrapped one has an orca-ide-app too,
+# minus nixGL.
+app=$(sed -nE 's|.*ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-([^}]*)\}.*|\1|p' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")
+if [ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# The GUI wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with its
+# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
+# wayland first, except in node mode or when the caller names a platform
+# itself -- `--ozone-platform` or `--ozone-platform=...` before any `--`,
+# the rule of Orca's own hasExplicitOzonePlatform; a -hint does not count.

+  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }

+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \

      makePackageWrapper =
        vendor: environment: pkg:
        if isNull cfg.packages then
          pkg
        else
          # Wrap the package's binaries with nixGL, while preserving the rest of
          # the outputs and derivation attributes.
          (pkg.overrideAttrs (old: {
            # Leave the name unchanged and rely on the hash to differentiate
            # from the original package. Some modules rely on the package name
            # to e.g. compute config directory paths.
            inherit (pkg) name;

            # Make sure this is false for the wrapper derivation, so nix doesn't expect
            # a new debug output to be produced. We won't be producing any debug info
            # for the original package.
            separateDebugInfo = false;
            nativeBuildInputs = old.nativeBuildInputs or [ ] ++ [ pkgs.makeWrapper ];
            buildCommand =
              let
                # We need an intermediate wrapper package because makeWrapper
                # requires a single executable as the wrapper.
                combinedWrapperPkg = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "nixGLCombinedWrapper-${vendor}" ''
                  exec ${getWrapperExe vendor} "$@"
                '';
              in
              ''
                set -eo pipefail

                ${
                  # Heavily inspired by https://stackoverflow.com/a/68523368/6259505
                  lib.concatStringsSep "\n" (
                    map (outputName: ''
                      echo "Copying output ${outputName}"
                      set -x
                      cp -rs --no-preserve=mode "${pkg.${outputName}}" "''$${outputName}"
                      set +x
                    '') (old.outputs or [ "out" ])
                  )
                }

                rm -rf $out/bin/*
                shopt -s nullglob # Prevent loop from running if no files
                for file in ${pkg.out}/bin/*; do
                  local prog="$(basename "$file")"
                  makeWrapper \
                    "${lib.getExe combinedWrapperPkg}" \
                    "$out/bin/$prog" \
                    --argv0 "$prog" \
                    --add-flags "$file" \
                    ${lib.concatStringsSep " " (
                      lib.attrsets.mapAttrsToList (var: val: "--set '${var}' '${val}'") environment
                    )}
                done

                # If .desktop files refer to the old package, replace the references
                for dsk in "$out/share/applications"/*.desktop ; do
                  if ! grep -q "${pkg.out}" "$dsk"; then
                    continue
                  fi
                  src="$(readlink "$dsk")"
                  rm "$dsk"
                  sed "s|${pkg.out}|$out|g" "$src" > "$dsk"

set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

Round 5 review of origin/master..HEAD (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, tests/sandbox-fonts.sh). I launched nothing and wrote nothing. I checked the claims against the extracted app JS in the scratchpad asar, the store's extracted AppImage (Electron 43.8.1, node v24.22.0), home-manager's nixgl.nix and nixpkgs' build-fhsenv-bubblewrap.

## Critical
None.

## Important

**orca.nix:35-38 (`dieWithParent = false`), with orca.nix:126-129. Stopping `orca-ide serve` with a signal can leave an orphaned Orca server running.**
- **How the signal travels.** `serve` (cli/runtime/launch.js `spawnElectronServe`) spawns ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE as its child. Every wrapper layer execs the next (nixGL wrapper, nixGLCombinedWrapper, nixGLIntel `exec "$@"`, orca-ide-app, `.orca-ide-unwrapped`'s `exec "${cmd[@]}"`), so the CLI's child pid is the outer bwrap. On SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP, `superviseForegroundServe` (cli/runtime/serve-update-supervisor.js:95-167) calls `child.kill('SIGTERM')`, then SIGKILL after a grace period.
- **Why that orphans the server.** bwrap does not forward signals. Its outer monitor process dies, and the sandboxed child gets no parent-death signal now that `--die-with-parent` is gone. The generated launchers here have no `--unshare-pid` either (that is buildFHSEnv's default). So the Electron server keeps running, holding the profile and port, while the CLI sees its child exit and returns.
- **What still works.** Ctrl-C in a terminal still reaches the server through the foreground process group, since there is no `--new-session`. Under a systemd service, the cgroup kill cleans up. The failure is `kill <cli>`, an agent's timeout, or anything else that signals the CLI's pid.
- **Before this branch.** With `dieWithParent = true` on master, the server would at least have been SIGKILLed with its parent. That path was not reachable on master, though, since the CLI dispatch was broken.
- **Comments.** The orca.nix:35-38 comment covers only the `open` side of this trade-off. "a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's own" (orca.nix:128) is true of the CLI but reads as if `serve` also stops cleanly. The commit message makes that contrast directly, against the branch that needed a signal forwarder.
- **Confidence.** I inferred this from bwrap's design (no signal forwarding, a parent-death signal only with `--die-with-parent`) and the generated launcher. I did not run it.
- **Options.**
  - Give `serve` a launcher with `dieWithParent = true`: a second wrapType2/FHS launcher that orca-ide-app execs when `--serve` is in argv. `open`'s detached GUI keeps the current one.
  - Or at least state the trade-off in the comment.
  - Either way, a test case should go red on whichever behaviour is chosen.

## nits
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:106.** `timeout 60` can still leave a process behind. If node mode works but the process hangs, timeout SIGTERMs only the outer bwrap, and the sandboxed node is orphaned with no die-with-parent. This is the same "timeout cannot reach past bwrap" problem the comment at :101-104 describes, and it only happens when something is already broken. Nothing hangs today, since `-p '"node-ok"'` exits at once. A more robust guard would be a self-exit inside the script (`-e 'setTimeout(()=>process.exit(1),N).unref(); ...'`), like the lifetime case's `process.exit` at 7s.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:32 and tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:37.** `$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n)` falls back only when the file is missing. An empty /etc/hostname gives `homeConfigurations..config`. This matters nowhere today (CI writes the file, and hosts have it); it is a robustness nit only.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:165 vs :171.** The rev check reads `.source` without `toString`, while the per-skill loop uses `toString`. Both work with `--raw`; this is a consistency nit only.

## Checked and found accurate (no finding)
- **The GUI wrapper's rule** (orca.nix:72-78) matches `hasExplicitOzonePlatform` in shared/headless-serve-ozone-platform.js, and main/index.js's `PEn`, exactly: bare `--ozone-platform` or `--ozone-platform=`, stop at `--`, and a `-hint` does not count.
- **The comment claims about serve:**
  - Serve appends `--ozone-platform=x11` (`headlessServeOzonePlatformSwitches`, after `--serve`).
  - Serve's runtime probe runs ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: '1'` and an entry script (serve-orcad-launch.js).
  - The serve-mode X11 restart (`FEn`) is skipped when `PEn(argv)` is true, so a hand-run `orca-ide-app --serve` stays on wayland, as the comment says.
- **The ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE comment** (orca.nix:133-136): `launchOrcaApp` throws `runtime_open_failed` and `resolveForegroundOrcaExecutable` throws `serverOnlyServeMessage` when neither ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE nor `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` is set. The NODE_OPTIONS handover matches upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide byte for byte. `openOrca` waits 15_000 ms, matching the test comment. Orca's terminal shim does not export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE into the terminal's environment, so the `:-` default is not overridden in Orca terminals.
- **The display gate runs before the single-instance lock** (`APn`: `isPackaged && !isServeMode && !dPn()` then exit 1). So a lost node mode under `nodisplay` exits without forwarding argv to a running Orca. No window can open from the probes, and `hPn` reads both WAYLAND_SOCKET and WAYLAND_DISPLAY, which `nodisplay` unsets.
- **The lifetime case** goes red with `--die-with-parent`: `bash -c` stays up 4s and bwrap's parent is that bash, or the sleep it execs. The node process exits on its own at 7s, so nothing outlives the test.
- **The argv harness:**
  - nixGL's makeWrapper output puts `/nix/store/...-orca-.../bin/orca-ide-app` as a space-delimited `--add-flags` argument, so the grep picks the inner script.
  - The harness refuses to run if the exec swap fails.
  - Each case fails on the regression it names (always-prepend, prefix match, ignoring `--`, ignoring node mode).
- **Profile layout:**
  - nixGL's `bin/*` glob skips the `.orca-ide-unwrapped` dotfile, which stays a symlink.
  - pname `orca` survives the nixGL `overrideAttrs`, so `pkg_attr orca` finds the wrapped GUI.
  - Nothing outside orca.nix and tests/ references `orca-ide`.
- **The skills:** the manifest lists ten skills, as "the bundled ten" says. `sourceCommit:\`e6f7fba5…\`` appears in app.asar in the form the grep expects. The skills are stubs that say `orca-ide` outside Orca terminals on Linux.
- **Secrets:** nothing prints env values. `outside` passes only variable names to `env -u`, there is no `set -x`, and failure messages print CLI output, `ls` and file contents only.
- **CI** (nix-eval.yml tests mode): every tool used (`paste`, `tr`, `seq`, `timeout`, `sha256sum`, `uname`, `jq`, sed/grep) is in the pinned shell. bwrap as root in the privileged container is fine, and `/tmp` is bound into the FHS env (it is not in `ignored`).
- **sandbox-fonts.sh:** the usage path (`readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide-app`, then dirname twice) gives the nixGL output, and the script's closure scan for `.orca-ide-unwrapped` still finds the launcher. The `orca-[0-9.]+` filter does not match `orca-cli-*`.

The generated launchers here have no `--unshare-pid` either (that is buildFHSEnv's default). So the Electron server keeps running, holding the profile and port, while the CLI sees its child exit and returns.
- **What still works.** Ctrl-C in a terminal still reaches the server through the foreground process group, since there is no `--new-session`. Under a systemd service, the cgroup kill cleans up. The failure is `kill <cli>`, an agent's timeout, or anything else that signals the CLI's pid.
- **Before this branch.** With `dieWithParent = true` on master, the server would at least have been SIGKILLed with its parent. That path was not reachable on master, though, since the CLI dispatch was broken.
- **Comments.** The orca.nix:35-38 comment covers only the `open` side of this trade-off. "a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's own" (orca.nix:128) is true of the CLI but reads as if `serve` also stops cleanly. The commit message makes that contrast directly, against the branch that needed a signal forwarder.
- **Confidence.** I inferred this from bwrap's design (no signal forwarding, a parent-death signal only with `--die-with-parent`) and the generated launcher. I did not run it.
- **Options.**
  - Give `serve` a launcher with `dieWithParent = true`: a second wrapType2/FHS launcher that orca-ide-app execs when `--serve` is in argv. `open`'s detached GUI keeps the current one.
  - Or at least state the trade-off in the comment.
  - Either way, a test case should go red on whichever behaviour is chosen.
